umdProfile.bioSummary: The bio (first person) describes about twenty years of interdisciplinary research that combines satellite remote sensing and models with socio-economic and demographic data to understand what drives food security, including the effects of conflict, climate and agricultural development on communities in Africa and Asia. It mentions Peace Corps service in Senegal in the early 1990s, more than 120 journal articles and two books, lead authorship of the 2015 USDA-published climate assessment report on global food security, and thirteen years at NASA Goddard's Biospheric Sciences Branch (first as a contractor, then as a civil servant). It lists service on the CGMS socio-economic benefits tiger team (2013-2015), the NSF Environmental Research and Education Advisory Committee (2010-2012) and, since 2017, the National Academies' Committee on Earth Sciences and Applications from Space, plus a part-time role as Chief Science Officer of 6th Grain. It names four research agendas: vegetation remote sensing for climate variability; how satellite data are used in decisions (pre-launch applications work for the Carbon Monitoring System, SMAP and ICESat-2); models of climate effects on acute malnutrition in Africa; and creating training data that turn remote sensing into actionable agricultural information. It also mentions a book in progress on digital tools, AI and machine learning in food production.

books.title: Famine Early Warning Systems and Remote Sensing Data
books.summary: The book explains how USAID's Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) uses satellite remote sensing to detect biophysical hazards such as drought and to judge their effects on people's lives and livelihoods. It shows how FEWS NET combines physical science, developed with USGS, NASA, NOAA and USDA, with social-science livelihood and market analysis, and uses case studies to show how crises are identified, documented and responded to.
books.coverNotes: Served from Springer Nature's own media CDN (the page's og:image is the w153 rendition). Saved the w306 rendition, 306x436 px. Larger renditions exist but look upscaled.

books.title: Food Security, Food Prices and Climate Variability
books.summary: Drawing on about a decade of the author's research, the book uses satellite measurements of growing-season variability to examine how weather and climate have affected agricultural production, staple food prices and access to food in food-insecure regions. It links global environmental change to local food-price swings and frames the analysis around how humanitarian organizations such as FEWS NET and the UN World Food Programme monitor and respond to food crises.
books.coverNotes: Publisher's own jacket image (the og:image on the Routledge page). Only 180x272 px; the larger 'amazonl'/'gblarge' paths return 403. The JPEG is CMYK (4 components); convert it to sRGB if any browser renders it wrongly.
